title: A larger source charge
hook: Change source charge magnitude and predict electric-field magnitude.
misconception: electric-field magnitude stays fixed when source charge magnitude doubles.
objective: Apply E = k·abs(q)/r² to compare electric-field magnitude when source charge magnitude changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a point charge observed at fixed distance in the same medium, E = k·abs(q)/r². When source charge magnitude doubles, electric-field magnitude becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model E = k·abs(q)/r²; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a point charge observed at fixed distance in the same medium, with a nonzero initial result. If source charge magnitude triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on electric-field magnitude?
recall.why: Apply E = k·abs(q)/r² under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
